graph.title: LEGO 7736-1 Coast Guard Quad Bike

edges.method: round plate studs into the underside anti-studs of the 2x6 plate (left end, plate built upside down)
round plate studs into the underside anti-studs of the 2x6 plate (right end, plate built upside down)
wheel-holder plate studs into the anti-studs under the round plate
wheel-holder plate studs into the anti-studs under the round plate
two thin clips of the flag clipped onto the antenna shaft
handlebar pin pressed into the clip of the 1x1 clip tile
wheel holder pin into wheel hole
wheel holder pin into wheel hole
wheel holder pin into wheel hole
wheel holder pin into wheel hole

notes: The minifigure on page 2 (head, helmet, visor, torso, legs) is not in the piece list, so it is not recorded and I did not count it as a step. If it counts as a sub-assembly step, every step number here goes up by 1.

Steps 1-3 build the 2x6 plate (p12) upside down. The round plates (p14, p15) and wheel holders (p18, p19) are added after it but sit below it in the finished model. A grid position plus a rule that supporters come from earlier steps cannot both hold here: in the finished frame p12 would rest on parts from later steps, and in the build frame the step 4+ plates would. So I kept p12 and everything built from step 4 on in the finished frame, and gave the four underside pieces position null with rests_on []. Their real connections to the underside of p12 are in other_joins. This is a deliberate exception, not an omission.

Step numbering: 1 plate, 2 round plates, 3 wheel holders, 4 end plates and side handles, 5 mudguards, 6 jumpers and grille, 7 slope and clip tile, 8 flag and antenna sub-assembly, 9 handlebars, 10 wheel and tyre sub-assembly (the wheels are fitted to the model in the last main step). The booklet draws some parts already in place in the picture before the step that adds them. I read those as added in the step shown by the arrows.

Coordinates are approximate and inferred from small isometric drawings. I took the left end as x=1-2 and the right end as x=5-6. Which handle plates and light plates go where, and which mudguard goes on which end, is a best guess. When placed, the round plates would sit at layer 1 and the wheel holders at layer 0 under the x=1-2 and x=5-6 ends.
The two left jumper plates carry the cheese slope and the clip tile on their single studs. The right mudguard takes the grille tile and one jumper, and the antenna sits on that jumper's stud.
